rationale: While interpreting the extended-window receipt I found a second, unrelated observation that I cannot yet explain and must not let stand as a claim: at index 0 of 2444815cf0d84e06917efa1091d12257 the demoted node's own GetConfiguration still reported itself as a Voter (near_node_self_voter true) while the leader's configuration and both far nodes already reported the demotion (voters 3, nonvoters 1, near_node_voter false), after a bounded settle loop that polled that node's view every 20ms for three seconds. A node's own view is the atomic copy written by setLatestConfiguration, which runs only when a configuration entry is appended (processConfigurationLogEntry from appendEntries), so the observation would mean that node had not appended the demotion entry while the other nodes had committed and applied it. I tried to reproduce it natively (not retained evidence) with the same construction and per-node timing three ways - waiting for the followers before demoting, demoting immediately, and the exact per-node timing of the extended-window run - and in every case all four nodes reported the change within 0-21ms. That makes the observation either a rare replication stall on that one peer or an artefact of that run, and the discriminator below is what would settle it; I am recording it as an open sourced question instead of attaching it to the VerifyLeader claim, whose evidence does not depend on it (the quorum used by quorumSize and verifyLeader is the leader's configuration, corroborated by both far nodes and by the earlier fixed experiment).

investigations.question: After a committed voter-to-non-voter transition, can a peer's own configuration view keep reporting the old suffrage for seconds while the other peers already report the change, and if so what makes that peer lag on the configuration entry?
investigations.hypothesis: A configuration entry updates a peer's latest configuration only when it is newly appended (appendEntries processes configuration entries of newEntries) or installed through a snapshot; a peer that has not appended the entry keeps reporting its previous configuration. If the leader's replication to one peer stalls - for example a stalled append pipeline that never re-enters RPC mode - that peer would keep the old view while the others commit and apply the change.
investigations.discriminator: Sample every node's own configuration view and LastIndex continuously (for example every 20ms) across the DemoteVoter call and for at least ten seconds afterwards, in the per-node timing used by the extended-window scenario, and repeat the run several times. A peer whose view stays old while its LastIndex also stops advancing would show a replication stall; a peer whose LastIndex has already passed the configuration index while its view stays old would instead point at the configuration-entry processing path; view and index converging within milliseconds in every run would leave the earlier single observation as an unexplained artefact.
